design.pairing: Same original_id, expression, partition and question. S is always the left endpoint.
design.semantic_reference: Existing exposed-author input judgments only; not formal semantic labels. Report constructed pairs and author-reference-eligible pairs separately. Retain all six poker pairs with unknown S membership.

statistics.probabilities: All three right-minus-left probability deltas; focal increase means strictly greater than zero, with no optimized threshold. Report magnitude, sign counts and class transition tables.
statistics.behavior: Reuse sealed yes/no/unknown judgments without rescoring. Record endpoint changes, source-answer AND target-answer, focal increase AND target behavior, and focal increase conditional on target behavior. Unknowns remain in eligible denominators.
statistics.bootstrap_unit: original_id; retain all available contrasts and A/B expressions for every sampled base, including repeated draws
statistics.bootstrap_interval: Percentile 2.5 and 97.5 percent. For unknown behavior, compute separate sampling intervals for lower and upper identification bounds. These intervals exclude judgment uncertainty and model/training randomness and do not establish population representativeness.
statistics.composition_audit: For I endpoints, report each base as both expressions probe-refuse, mixed, or neither; report outcomes within mixed bases separately. For all eight variants, count stable class predictions and S/K conflict concentration by base. These are observational diagnostics, not adjustment proving causation.

boundaries: All source outputs and author judgments have already been viewed. This is a new post-hoc analysis, not preregistration or prospective confirmation.
No new scoring, semantic accuracy/MacroF1, training trigger, model/probe loading, generation, causal intervention, external reviewer or held-out 380-question access.
Source partitions are descriptive provenance only. Preserve frozen code, source run, prior reports, labels and gates.
